title: L'Imperfetto
subtitle: Italian's other past tense — for background, habits, and descriptions.
objectives: Conjugate regular verbs in the imperfetto
Conjugate the three key irregular imperfetto verbs: essere, fare, bere
Use the imperfetto for habitual past actions and descriptions

content.intro: While the passato prossimo reports a completed event, the imperfetto paints the background: what things were like, what used to happen, what was already going on.
content.explanation: The imperfetto is one of the most regular tenses in Italian — nearly every verb (even most that are irregular elsewhere) follows the same pattern, built by dropping -re from the infinitive and adding the imperfetto endings. Only essere is truly irregular; fare and bere use their old Latin stems (facere, bevere) rather than the modern infinitive.

rules.heading: a) Regular pattern
rules.body: Drop -are/-ere/-ire, add: -vo, -vi, -va, -vamo, -vate, -vano (with the conjugation's vowel kept: parla-vo, cred-e-vo, dorm-i-vo).

rules.heading: b) When to use the imperfetto
rules.body:
• Habitual/repeated past actions: Da bambino giocavo sempre fuori. (As a child I always used to play outside.)
  • Descriptions (people, places, weather, time, age) in the past: Era una bella giornata. Faceva caldo.
  • Background action interrupted by another (paired with passato prossimo, next lesson): Dormivo quando hai chiamato.

examples.en: As a child I lived in the countryside.
Every summer we would go to the seaside.
It was nine in the evening.
It was very cold that day.

examples.it: Mia nonna raccontava sempre storie bellissime.
examples.en: My grandmother always used to tell wonderful stories.

commonMistakes.wrong: Ieri sono andato al mare ogni giorno.
commonMistakes.why: A repeated/habitual action needs the imperfetto, not the passato prossimo, which reports a single completed event.
Age uses avere alone (avevo), not combined with essere.

commonMistakes.wrong: Fecevo i compiti ogni sera. (for fare)
commonMistakes.why: Fare's imperfetto stem is fac- (from facere), giving facevo, not a form based on the modern infinitive fare.

items.prompt: Da bambina, io ___ (giocare) sempre in giardino.

items.explanation: Essere's irregular imperfetto io form is ero.

items.prompt: Noi ___ (avere) un cane quando ero piccolo.
Describing what the weather was like yesterday afternoon:
items.explanation: Weather description in the past uses the imperfetto.

items.prompt: Tu ___ (bere) sempre il caffè la mattina, da giovane.
Noi ___ (fare) i compiti insieme ogni pomeriggio.
items.explanation: Fare's imperfetto stem is fac-: facevamo.

items.prompt: Quando ero piccolo, mio padre mi ___ (leggere) sempre una storia.
Which sentence describes a habitual past action?
options: Da bambino andavo spesso al cinema.
Sono andato al cinema una volta.
items.explanation: A repeated habit in the past needs the imperfetto.

items.prompt: Which verb is truly irregular in the imperfetto?
items.explanation: Essere alone is truly irregular; fare/bere just use an old stem with regular endings.

items.statement: The imperfetto is one of the most regular tenses in Italian.
items.explanation: Nearly every verb follows the same pattern in the imperfetto.

items.statement: Fare's imperfetto is built from its modern infinitive, giving "farevo".
items.explanation: Fare's imperfetto is built from the old stem facere, giving facevo.

summary: The imperfetto is built regularly: stem + -vo/-vi/-va/-vamo/-vate/-vano; only essere is truly irregular.
Use it for habitual past actions, descriptions, and background states.
Contrast with the passato prossimo, which reports single, completed events — next lesson.
